title: Waymo takes Tampa passengers into oncoming NFL game traffic: Video
key_facts: A group of young men abandoned a driverless Waymo after it took them into oncoming traffic outside Raymond James Stadium during last Sunday's Buccaneers game.
The car drove north on North Himes Avenue, which had been redirected for southbound traffic at that moment.
A passenger's TikTok video and a second video sent to WFLA show the passengers alarmed; the stuck Waymo was then seen blocking a lane.
It appears the car did not know traffic on Himes had been redirected.
A Waymo spokesperson said a vehicle 'briefly entered a temporary one-way street before correcting the issue' and that Waymo is looking into the event.
In July a driverless Tesla Robotaxi was seen going the wrong way a day after Tampa launch, but on a road that is always one-way.
quote_evidence: A group of young men ended up having to abandon their driverless Waymo after it took them into oncoming traffic outside of Raymond James Stadium during last Sunday’s Buccaneers game.
It appears that the driverless vehicle was not aware that traffic was redirected on Himes and was heading north as if it were a normal travel route.
In Tampa this week, a Waymo vehicle briefly entered a temporary one-way street before correcting the issue.
why_it_matters_hint: Driverless cars can miss temporary traffic changes around big events, which puts passengers and other road users at risk.
event_date: 'Last Sunday' relative to a 9 Oct 2026 publication, so about 4 Oct 2026 (inferred, the article gives no date)
notes: Story is WFLA's reporting carried by NewsNation (WFLA is the NewsNation affiliate named in the dateline). No injury is mentioned. The passengers' video describes the car as still blocking a lane, which sits uneasily with Waymo's 'briefly'.
